partners.mechanism_chain: FN1 (HGNC:3720) —DISRUPTS→ Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, 'corner fracture' type (MONDO:0008479); PLG (HGNC:9074) —INCREASES→ Complement system activation (GO:0006955); Complement system activation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ Angioedema, hereditary, 4 (MONDO:0025712); Complement system activation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, 'corner fracture' type (MONDO:0008479). Loss-of-function mutations in FN1 lead to spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, 'corner fracture' type. **Proposed mechanism:** Fibronectin 1 (HGNC:3277) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, 'corner fracture' type (MONDO:0008479); Amyloid beta precursor protein (HGNC:651) —DISRUPTS→ Amyloid deposition (GO:0000285); Amyloid deposition (GO:0000285) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebral amyloid angiopathy, APP-related (MONDO:0011583); Amyloid beta precursor protein (HGNC:651) —BINDS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198). Haploinsufficiency of FN1 disrupts extracellular matrix organization, leading to spondylometaphyseal dysplasia. Gain-of-function mutations in APP lead to amyloid deposition, causing cerebral amyloid angiopathy. Crucially, APP also interacts with and influences extracellular matrix organization, providing a point of convergence.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of any interaction or shared downstream pathway between APP and extracellular matrix components, or evidence that FN1 mutations do not impact ECM organization. _(variant: rs113700131)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of APP in both amyloidosis and potentially ECM regulation could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both neurodegenerative diseases and skeletal dysplasias, particularly those involving ECM defects.
